package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The article discusses the scale, security, and governance challenges of open source package consumption, but does not analyze or identify any particular malicious code or package.

behavioral_signatures: High-volume automated downloads by CI/CD systems
Inclusion of outdated or unmaintained packages
Use of packages with known vulnerabilities
file_indicators: Presence of old or deprecated JavaScript libraries (e.g., YUI, SWFObject)
Multiple versions of the same package cached in local repositories
network_indicators: Frequent outbound requests to public package registries (e.g., registry.npmjs.org)
Automated download patterns from CI/CD IP ranges
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the use of outdated or unmaintained packages, especially those with known vulnerabilities. Implement repository health checks and automated policy enforcement to block or flag vulnerable components. Track high-frequency download patterns that may indicate automated build systems or potential abuse. Regularly audit dependency trees for security issues and ensure that only approved, up-to-date packages are used in production.
